mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month indicates a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants react to the news.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS shows a sustained increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the same month, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it indicates inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter signals strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.
